hints.tr: `fig, (sol, sag) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 4))` iki çizim alanı veriyor.
hints.en: `fig, (left, right) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 4))` gives you two drawing areas.

hints.tr: Her alan ayrı bir eksen: `sol.bar(...)`, `sag.scatter(...)`. Başlıkları da ayrı ayrı veriyorsun.
hints.en: Each area is its own axes: `left.bar(...)`, `right.scatter(...)`. You set their titles separately too.

hints.tr: Tuvaldeki alan sayısını `len(fig.axes)` veriyor. `fig.tight_layout()` alanların birbirine girmesini engelliyor.
hints.en: `len(fig.axes)` gives the number of areas on the canvas. `fig.tight_layout()` stops them overlapping.

hints.tr:
Çözüm:

```python
fig, (sol, sag) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 4))

sol.bar(data["city"], data["score"])
sol.set_ylim(0, 100)
sol.set_title("Scores")

sag.scatter(data["hours"], data["score"])
sag.set_title("Hours vs score")
sag.set_xlabel("Hours")

fig.tight_layout()

print(len(fig.axes))
print(len(sol.patches))
print(sol.get_title(), "|", sag.get_title())
print(int(sol.get_ylim()[1]))
```
hints.en:
The solution:

```python
fig, (left, right) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 4))

left.bar(data["city"], data["score"])
left.set_ylim(0, 100)
left.set_title("Scores")

right.scatter(data["hours"], data["score"])
right.set_title("Hours vs score")
right.set_xlabel("Hours")

fig.tight_layout()

print(len(fig.axes))
print(len(left.patches))
print(left.get_title(), "|", right.get_title())
print(int(left.get_ylim()[1]))
```
